title: Console telemetry Eraser Service: ephemeral ID mapping & PII retention enforcer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an "Eraser Service" in the console backend that enforces retention windows and removes PII from streaming & batch telemetry. The service should: 1) store only ephemeral identifiers for user-facing telemetry (hashed+salted ephemeral IDs mapped to a revocable token), 2) provide safe deletion and rollback for retention and legal-hold scenarios, 3) integrate with existing analytics pipelines (batch ETL + streaming Kafka topics) to scrub PII at ingestion and at rest, 4) produce auditable deletion manifests and retention metrics for Compliance and Support. This ticket covers the backend service, API surface, dataflow adapters for streaming and batch jobs, and a small admin console page to kick off manual erasure and view manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Eraser Service exposes an authenticated REST API to request erasure by ephemeral_id or by policy (age, label, org)
Telemetry ingestion adapters redact configured PII fields before writing raw events into long-term storage (S3/GCS) and mark records with ephemeral_id
Mapping store implements a revocable ephemeral_id <-> subject hash mapping encrypted at rest using KMS and supports TTL-based automatic rotation
Deletion workflow runs produce signed manifests listing removed object keys and counts and are retained for audit per policy
There is a safe rollback path for false-positive deletions (grace window + tombstone metadata) documented and covered by tests
Retention enforcement worker runs at configured cadence and respects legal-hold flags that prevent deletion
End-to-end integration tests simulate streaming ingestion, scrubbing, and deletion and assert no PII remains in downstream analytics tables after enforcement
SLO: erasure requests complete within 60s for up to 10k event keys; retention worker throughput metric documented in the Console dashboard
tasks: Design mapping store schema and encryption model (KMS/HSM)
Implement Eraser Service REST API + auth (mTLS + token)
Add streaming adapter to redact configured PII fields on Kafka consumer side
Instrument batch ETL jobs to run pre-commit scrubbing for legacy tables
Implement retention enforcement worker with legal-hold checks and manifest generation
Create admin console page (internal) to trigger ad-hoc erasure and show manifests
Add auditing events (who requested, scope, manifest SHA) to secure audit log
Write integration and load tests, run canary on staging cluster
design_notes: Prefer ephemeral identifiers: generate ephemeral_id = HMAC(salt || subject_hash || rotation_epoch) to avoid storing raw PII; store mapping encrypted with KMS and a per-tenant wrapping key
Scrubbing will be rule-driven: rules defined in Console (field name, regex, transform) and deployed to ingestion adapters via config rolls
Use tombstones for 48h soft-delete window before final purge to allow rollback for operator errors
Legal-hold flag stored in policy service; retention worker must query policy service before purge
Manifests are uploaded to an immutable audit bucket (write-once) and manifest metadata is reflected in the Console audit panel
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental over-deletion due to misconfigured scrubbing rules. Mitigation: require two-step approval for global scrubbing rule changes and run dry-run mode on staging data
Risk: mapping store compromise exposing subject links. Mitigation: encrypt mappings with tenant-specific KEKs and rotate keys quarterly; limit access via RBAC and VPC restrictions
Risk: retention worker performance causing backlog. Mitigation: sharded worker architecture + backpressure metrics + autoscaling for enforcement workers
Risk: downstream analytics caches retain PII. Mitigation: add purge hooks for common downstream stores and a verification job that scans known tables for residual PII patterns
implementation_notes: Language: Go service running in Console backend cluster; container image built with distroless base
Mapping store: DynamoDB (low-latency reads) + S3 for large object manifests; use envelope encryption with KMS
Streaming adapter: Kafka Streams consumer that applies scrubbing rules before writing to raw-topic-consumer output
Batch integration: pre-commit lambda for EMR/Spark jobs to apply scrubbing to exported parquet files
Errors: store failed deletion items in quarantine bucket for manual review with two-person escalation
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping generation, encryption/decryption, and policy checks
Integration tests hooking Eraser Service to a local Kafka + DynamoDB test environment
End-to-end test: simulate telemetry containing sample PII, run scrubbing + retention worker, and assert no PII in S3/warehouse
Chaos test: kill worker during a manifest generation, ensure resume idempotency
Load test: simulate 5M event/day retention enforcement run and measure worker latency
rollout_plan: Feature flagged rollout per-tenant; enable scrubbing in dry-run mode initially (produce manifests but do not delete)
Run for 2 weeks in dry-run for 10 pilot tenants, compare manifests to manual audit
Enable soft-delete tombstone phase for next 2 weeks, continue monitoring
Enable final purge for pilot tenants after signoff, then expand by 10x cohorts
Post-rollout: run 30-day audit and publish internal compliance report
metrics_and_success: Primary: percent of telemetry events with PII removed at ingestion (>99.9%)
Operational: retention_worker_backlog under threshold and manifest_generation_latency < 120s
Compliance: audit manifests retained and retrievable for all deletion events (100%)
